tools.name: what_can_you_do
tools.description: Describe a task in plain language (any language) and get back exactly which tools on this server do it, with ready-to-run example calls — instead of reading the whole catalogue and guessing. Also returns multi-step recipes when a task needs several tools chained (invoices to a ledger, a bank stateme

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: List the open-source AI applications hosted and ready to run at AI NetCafé (ainetcafe.com). Each one normally requires local setup (Docker/Python + your own model API key); here they run pre-configured. Use this to find a tool for a task like translating a PDF with formulas intact, generating a Powe

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: Full details of one hosted application: what it does, how to use it, measured benchmark scores, source repository, and the URL a human can open to run it. Example — GET https://ainetcafe.com/t/get_app?slug=<slug-from-list_apps>

tools.name: submit_project
tools.description: Submit a GitHub repository (a web app, typically AI-built) to the AI NetCafé hosting platform. The automated pipeline reviews it, containerizes it, deploys it on a dedicated subdomain with HTTPS and a pre-wired multi-LLM gateway, lists it in the store for humans, and exposes it to AI agents. tools.name: project_status
tools.description: Check where a repository stands on AI NetCafé: live (with its public page and app URL), in the deployment pipeline, rejected (with the reason), or unknown. Use after submit_project. Example — GET https://ainetcafe.com/t/project_status?repo=<owner/name>

tools.name: check_job
tools.description: Get the status or result of a job started by deep_research, translate_pdf, or make_slides. Poll every 15-30 seconds until status is "done" or "error". While work is pending, follow retry_after_seconds and next_action; when complete, prefer structured_result when present. Example — GET https://ainetc

tools.name: build_app
tools.description: Turn one plain-language description into a LIVE single-page web tool: code is generated, deployed to managed hosting with HTTPS, and listed — you get the public URL in ~1-2 minutes. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "build?s=registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_app, project_status, build_app · Private data: list_apps · Public sink: submit_project · Destructive: what_can_you_do, list_apps, get_app.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_app, project_status, build_app · Private data: list_apps · Public sink: submit_project · Destructive: what_can_you_do, list_apps, get_app

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_apps" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
